# Promobeez

> Promobeez connects local businesses with nano and micro-creators through barter deals — a coffee for a post, a haircut for a reel. No cash commissions. Made in Helsinki by Daring Spirit Oy.

Promobeez is a barter marketplace for neighbourhood businesses and creators from 500 followers. Businesses post offers (product or service in exchange for content); creators apply with real audience stats and geo. Contacts unlock only when both sides match. Creators are always free; businesses pay only to unlock more offers and contacts.

Primary market: Helsinki / Finland. App signup: https://my.promobeez.com

## Key claims from the evidence reviews

### Trust premium (small creators vs brand ads)
- Recommendations from people you know (~88% trust in Nielsen) far outperform ads from influencers (~23%); the gap is perceived motive, not the medium.
- Brand self-promotion triggers persuasion knowledge; small creators sit closer to peer recommendation.
- Edelman 2026: trust is relocating toward neighbours, family and coworkers while national institutions lose ground.
- Micro-influencers who disclose can outperform macros who hide sponsorship; similarity and trust mediate outcomes more than category fit alone.
- Do not scale one nano into a permanent ad channel — the “influencer” label itself erodes trust.

### Local creators vs fame
- Smaller creators do not win because they are small; they win when audience, credibility, content and economics match the campaign objective.
- A 2024 Journal of Marketing study (Beichert et al.) found lower-followership Instagram creators delivered higher revenue per follower and return on influencer spend in a DTC setting — exact multipliers should not be treated as universal for every local business.
- For restaurants and local services, commercially relevant (local) reach matters more than total follower count.
- Micro-influencers often score higher on trust, similarity and authenticity; larger creators can still win for awareness, prestige or popular brands.
- In Finland, gifted meals/services used for advertising require clear disclosure (KKV Consumer Ombudsman guidance).
